summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandra R. de Silva (1940–2021) was a historian and archaeologist. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (attested 1991) and as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1957–1960), held a post there (~1960–1974), and served as a professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1974–1994).

Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and doctoral supervisor Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura, and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He was a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo (1899–1958) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Northwest University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Xiamen University, before serving at Peking University (~1929–1949).

Chanju Mun (1964–) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002), supervised by Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda, and taught by John D. Dunne.

Channa Li works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Leiden University under Jonathan A. Silk, becoming a PhD candidate by 2019, and is attested as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Chao-heng Liao specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Roy Rappaport and completed her PhD under Norma Diamond at the University of Michigan by 1999, later becoming an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who earned his AB and PhD at Yale University. He served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967) and founded and edited the journal Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell (1870–1945) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College (~1889–1891).

Charles B. Jones works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner by 1996 and served as an associate professor and associate dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

Charles Bally (1865–1947) was a Swiss linguist. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1891–1913), later serving at the University of Geneva (~1893–1939).

Charles Burnett (1951–) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. After earning his BA and doctorate at the University of Cambridge, he held research positions before serving as lecturer and professor (from 1999) at the Warburg Institute.

Charles Cutler Torrey (1863–1956) was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900) and was a professor at Yale University (1900–1932).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (attested 1998–2006).

Charles DiSimone works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his PhD from the University of Munich by 2016, he held a post there (attested 2021) and serves as a co-director and permanent member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a superintendent for the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940) and Burma Circle (ASI), and as a professor at the University of Rangoon (~1920).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura (1907–1977) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology. He earned multiple degrees including a PhD and D.Litt. from the University of London, taught at SOAS (~1953–1959), and was Commissioner of Archaeology (1956–1967).
